findings.detail: 35 increments, all finite, stress responding to strain
original and converted agree to 3.210e-16 in stress and 2.158e-16 in state over 35 increments
the reported tangent is the derivative of the re-evaluated update at all 34 increments carried (worst 5.858e-11 at increment 10); the secant across increments, which is not a derivative, was not used
dR/dEQPLAS agrees to 8.328e-12 at h=0.001, over a plateau of 6 step sizes (0.001 to 1e-08)
dR/dH agrees to 6.699e-11 at h=0.0001, over a plateau of 6 step sizes (0.001 to 1e-08)

6 components as 3 direct and 3 engineering shear, and the tangent is shaped and signed accordingly, over a window whose largest shear strain is 1.000e+00 of its largest extension -- enough that a factor of two would show

a constant stress integrates to its surface tractions (1.960e-16), a linearly varying one to an independent target (2.184e-14) -- which is what tests the stress-to-point pairing -- and a rigid translation strains nothing (1.110e-16)
B^T sigma integrates to the independent reference within 0.000e+00, and the nodal forces of a uniform stress cancel to 4.862e-16 of their own size
B^T D B is the derivative of the element force with the increment-5 tangent: agrees to 3.598e-13 at h=0.01, over a plateau of 5 step sizes (0.01 to 1e-06)
step 1 prescribes 24 of 24 degrees of freedom and leaves 0 free, a partition with no overlap; reading the deck's steps as one flat list would get 0 of them wrong
24 global rows, one per (node, component), dense and without collision, and every element gathers the rows its own connectivity resolves to (highest row used: 23)
